accepted.s: Which one of the following bodies was associated with the year 1962 in the history of poverty estimation in India?
o: NITI Aayog Task Force on Elimination of Poverty
Expert Group chaired by D.T. Lakdawala
accepted.x: The Planning Commission Working Group was associated with poverty estimation in 1962. The Task Force on Minimum Needs was constituted in 1979, while the Lakdawala Expert Group and NITI Aayog Task Force belong to later years.
accepted.tq: Use the year-body association and eliminate bodies belonging to later periods.
accepted.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who among the following authored the study titled ‘Poverty in India’ published in 1971?
o: Suresh D. Tendulkar and C. Rangarajan
accepted.x: The 1971 study ‘Poverty in India’ was authored by V.M. Dandekar and N. Rath.
accepted.tq: Test the author-work association directly.
accepted.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Task Force on Minimum Needs, constituted in 1979, was chaired by:
accepted.x: The 1979 Task Force on Minimum Needs was chaired by Y.K. Alagh.
accepted.tq: Match the committee year with its chairperson.
accepted.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following committees and groups:
1. Planning Commission Working Group
2. Dandekar-Rath study
3. Task Force on Minimum Needs
4. Tendulkar Expert Group
Which of the following is the correct chronological order?
accepted.x: The correct sequence is 1962 Working Group, 1971 Dandekar-Rath study, 1979 Task Force on Minimum Needs and 2005 Tendulkar Expert Group.
accepted.tq: Identify the earliest and latest items first, then arrange the middle items by year.
accepted.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Expert Group chaired by D.T. Lakdawala submitted its report in which year, although it was accepted in 1997?
accepted.x: The Lakdawala Expert Group submitted its report in 1993, and its recommendations were accepted in 1997.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the report year from the year of acceptance.
accepted.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The NITI Aayog Task Force on Elimination of Poverty, constituted in 2015, was chaired by:
accepted.x: The 2015 NITI Aayog Task Force on Elimination of Poverty was chaired by Arvind Panagariya.
accepted.tq: Test the chairperson-task force association.
accepted.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following early poverty estimates is correctly matched?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji — ₹75 per year in 1944 prices
National Planning Committee — ₹15–20 per month in 1938
Bombay Plan — ₹16–35 per capita per year in 1867–68 prices
accepted.x: The National Planning Committee proposed ₹15–20 per month in 1938. Dadabhai Naoroji’s estimate related to 1867–68 prices, while the Bombay Plan proposed ₹75 per year in 1944.
accepted.tq: Check each historical estimate against both its year and monetary unit.
accepted.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Dadabhai Naoroji’s early poverty estimate was expressed at 1867–68 prices as:
accepted.x: Dadabhai Naoroji estimated poverty at ₹16–35 per capita per year at 1867–68 prices.
accepted.tq: Focus on the historical figure and distinguish annual from monthly estimates.
accepted.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which committee used a poverty norm of 2,250 kcal per day for both rural and urban areas?
accepted.x: The Dandekar-Rath study used 2,250 kcal per day as the nutritional norm for both rural and urban areas.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar calorie-based committee recommendations.
accepted.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the calorie norms associated with the Alagh Task Force?
o: 2,155 kcal for rural and 2,090 kcal for urban areas
2,400 kcal for rural and 2,100 kcal for urban areas
2,100 kcal for rural and 2,400 kcal for urban areas
2,250 kcal for rural and urban areas alike
accepted.x: The Alagh Task Force prescribed 2,400 kcal per day for rural areas and 2,100 kcal per day for urban areas.
accepted.tq: Compare the rural and urban values rather than recalling only one figure.
accepted.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lakdawala methodology:
1. It retained the calorie basis of poverty estimation.
2. It used State-specific poverty lines.
3. It used CPI-AL for rural areas and CPI-IW for urban areas.
4. It continued scaling poverty estimates to National Accounts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Lakdawala approach stopped scaling poverty estimates to National Accounts.
accepted.tq: Find the single incorrect methodological feature among closely related statements.
accepted.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was a significant change introduced by the Tendulkar methodology?
o: Replacement of MRP by URP for all items
Use of one urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas
Removal of private health expenditure from consumption
accepted.x: The Tendulkar methodology used one urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas. It moved away from an exclusive calorie anchor, included private health and education expenditure, and used MRP in place of URP.
accepted.tq: Identify the methodological reform and reject reversed or extreme alternatives.
accepted.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Rangarajan poverty estimation methodology?
o: Use of calorie, protein and fat norms
Use of a single urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas
Separate treatment of food and non-food requirements
accepted.x: The single urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas was associated with Tendulkar. Rangarajan used separate food and non-food requirements, nutritional norms and MMRP data.
accepted.tq: Identify the method belonging to the neighbouring committee.
accepted.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Rangarajan methodology prescribed calorie norms of:
o: 2,400 kcal for rural areas and 2,100 kcal for urban areas
2,155 kcal for rural areas and 2,090 kcal for urban areas
2,250 kcal for rural and urban areas alike
2,090 kcal for rural areas and 2,155 kcal for urban areas
accepted.x: Rangarajan used 2,155 kcal for rural areas and 2,090 kcal for urban areas, along with protein and fat norms.
accepted.tq: Separate close numerical values by assigning them to the correct area.
accepted.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes URP from MRP?
o: URP uses a 30-day recall period for all items, whereas MRP uses 365 days for selected low-frequency items.
URP uses a 365-day recall period for every item, whereas MRP uses 30 days for every item.
MRP is used only for urban poverty estimation.
Both URP and MRP use only annual income data.
accepted.x: URP uses a 30-day recall period for all items. MRP uses a 365-day recall period for five low-frequency items such as clothing, footwear, durables, education and institutional medical care.
accepted.tq: Split the two recall-period concepts by comparing their time spans and coverage.
accepted.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the National Multidimensional Poverty Index, the three dimensions are equally weighted. Which of the following is NOT one of these dimensions?
accepted.x: The National MPI has three equally weighted dimensions: health, education and standard of living. Employment security is not listed as one of the three dimensions.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated three-part structure.
accepted.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s National Multidimensional Poverty Index is estimated by:
o: The Finance Commission in association with the World Bank
NITI Aayog in association with UNDP and OPHI
accepted.x: India’s National MPI is estimated by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this function?’ method to identify the estimating body.
accepted.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a standard-of-living indicator in India’s National MPI?
accepted.x: Standard-of-living indicators include cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets and bank accounts.
accepted.tq: Classify the indicator under the correct MPI dimension.
accepted.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Progress Review 2023 covering NFHS-4 to NFHS-5, India’s multidimensional poverty headcount ratio changed from:
accepted.x: The headcount ratio declined from 24.85% in 2015–16 to 14.96% in 2019–21 under the Progress Review 2023.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the report period and pair the figures in the correct direction.
accepted.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the NITI Discussion Paper of January 2024, approximately how many people exited multidimensional poverty over nine years?
accepted.x: The paper estimated that 24.82 crore people exited multidimensional poverty over the nine-year period.
accepted.tq: Separate the national nine-year estimate from the Progress Review and State-wise figures.
accepted.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State recorded the largest fall in the number of multidimensionally poor people?
accepted.x: Uttar Pradesh recorded the largest fall, involving 5.94 crore people, followed by Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.
accepted.tq: Rank the State-wise figures by identifying the largest value.
accepted.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of the fall in the number of multidimensionally poor people:
A. Rajasthan
B. Uttar Pradesh
C. Madhya Pradesh
D. Bihar
accepted.x: The correct order is Uttar Pradesh (5.94 crore), Bihar (3.77 crore), Madhya Pradesh (2.30 crore) and Rajasthan (1.87 crore).
accepted.tq: Arrange the items by ranking their numerical values from highest to lowest.
accepted.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the 2011–12 poverty-line estimates, which of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Tendulkar urban poverty line was ₹1,000 per month, not ₹1,407. The Rangarajan rural and urban lines were ₹972 and ₹1,407 respectively.
accepted.tq: Match each committee with the correct rural or urban monthly figure.
accepted.sec: Rangarajan and Tendulkar poverty lines - figures, ratios for 2011-12  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Tendulkar poverty line for rural areas in 2011–12 was approximately equivalent to:
accepted.x: The Tendulkar rural poverty line was ₹816 per month, approximately ₹27 per day.
accepted.tq: Convert or recognise the monthly and daily equivalents of the same poverty line.
accepted.sec: Rangarajan and Tendulkar poverty lines - figures, ratios for 2011-12  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the all-India poverty ratio under the Tendulkar estimates for 2011–12?
accepted.x: The Tendulkar all-India poverty ratio was 21.9%; the rural ratio was 25.7% and the urban ratio was 13.7%.
accepted.tq: Keep the all-India, rural and urban ratios in their proper columns.
accepted.sec: Rangarajan and Tendulkar poverty lines - figures, ratios for 2011-12  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The all-India poverty ratio recommended by the Rangarajan methodology for 2011–12 was:
accepted.x: The Rangarajan methodology estimated the all-India poverty ratio at 29.5% for 2011–12.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Rangarajan all-India ratio from the Tendulkar ratios.
accepted.sec: Rangarajan and Tendulkar poverty lines - figures, ratios for 2011-12  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the Tendulkar and Rangarajan poverty-line figures is correct?
o: The Rangarajan urban line was lower than the Tendulkar urban line.
The Rangarajan rural and urban lines were ₹972 and ₹1,407 per month respectively.
The Tendulkar rural line was ₹972 per month.
Both committees prescribed identical rural and urban poverty lines.
accepted.x: The Rangarajan poverty lines were ₹972 per month for rural areas and ₹1,407 per month for urban areas. These were higher than the corresponding Tendulkar lines of ₹816 and ₹1,000.
accepted.tq: Use reversed-comparison traps to compare both committees’ figures.
accepted.sec: Rangarajan and Tendulkar poverty lines - figures, ratios for 2011-12  [APPSC]

accepted.s: N.C. Saxena’s report of August 2009 was primarily concerned with:
o: Preparing the rural BPL Census methodology
accepted.x: N.C. Saxena’s report, prepared for the Ministry of Rural Development, dealt with the method for the rural BPL Census rather than poverty estimation itself.
accepted.tq: Separate BPL identification from poverty-line estimation.
accepted.sec: Abhijit Sen / Saxena / Hashim - BPL identification vs methodology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was proposed as an example of automatic inclusion in the rural BPL identification approach associated with N.C. Saxena?
accepted.x: The proposed automatic-inclusion categories included PVTGs, single-woman-headed households, destitute and homeless households, and bonded labourers. Income-tax payers were examples of automatic exclusion.
accepted.tq: Distinguish automatic inclusion from automatic exclusion categories.
accepted.sec: Abhijit Sen / Saxena / Hashim - BPL identification vs methodology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Planning Commission working group associated with the identification of urban BPL families was chaired by:
accepted.x: S.R. Hashim headed the Planning Commission working group concerned with identifying urban BPL families.
accepted.tq: Match the expert with the specific BPL-identification task.
accepted.sec: Abhijit Sen / Saxena / Hashim - BPL identification vs methodology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between poverty estimation and BPL identification?
o: N.C. Saxena dealt with rural BPL Census methodology, while S.R. Hashim dealt with urban BPL identification.
S.R. Hashim dealt with rural BPL identification, while N.C. Saxena dealt with the Global MPI.
N.C. Saxena’s work estimated the national poverty ratio, while Hashim’s work fixed calorie norms.
Both N.C. Saxena and S.R. Hashim dealt exclusively with National MPI estimation.
accepted.x: N.C. Saxena’s work concerned the rural BPL Census methodology, whereas S.R. Hashim’s working group addressed identification of urban BPL families.
accepted.tq: Compare the jurisdiction and purpose of two easily confused expert groups.
accepted.sec: Abhijit Sen / Saxena / Hashim - BPL identification vs methodology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Data for poverty estimation traditionally came from NSS consumer expenditure rounds, which were generally conducted once every:
accepted.x: NSS consumer expenditure rounds were traditionally conducted every five years. The more recent data sources include HCES 2022–23 and 2023–24.
accepted.tq: Recall the periodicity of the survey rather than the latest survey years.
accepted.sec: Data and price indices  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the Lakdawala method, poverty lines were updated using which combination of price indices?
o: CPI-AL for rural areas and CPI-IW for urban areas
WPI for rural areas and CPI-IW for urban areas
GDP deflator for rural areas and WPI for urban areas
CPI-IW for rural areas and CPI-AL for urban areas
accepted.x: The Lakdawala method used the Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL) for rural areas and the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) for urban areas.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the rural and urban price-index assignments.
accepted.sec: Data and price indices  [other exams]

accepted.s: The RBI’s 2025 update of the Rangarajan poverty line using HCES 2022–23 relied on:
o: A new index based on PLB food and non-food weights
The plain CPI without any weighting change
accepted.x: The RBI update used a new index constructed from poverty-line basket food and non-food weights, rather than the plain CPI.
accepted.tq: Identify the index-construction basis and reject the familiar but incorrect plain-CPI option.
accepted.sec: Data and price indices  [other exams]
